heard: A subatomic particle hit Earth with the energy of a fast-pitched baseball. In October 1991, the fly's eye detector in Utah captured a visitor traveling at nearly light speed. Dubbed the oh-my-god particle, this single proton packed 320 exalectron volts of energy. That is 47 million times more energy than our most powerful human-built accelerators. Most people assume such force must come from a massive, visible cosmic engine. But tracing its path back reveals absolutely nothing in the darkness where it began. In 2021, the Amaterasu particle arrived with similar power from a completely empty cosmic void. These invisible missiles prove the universe can hit us with the energy of a fast-pitched baseball.
